$comment: RF-2 — provenance manifest. Each entry pins the sha256 of a file whose silent edit would invalidate a recorded, live-verified assertion. Verified by scripts/verify-provenance.mjs on every test run (working tree) and by .githooks/pre-commit (index). Re-baseline ONLY with --update, in the same commit as the change, so a reviewer sees both halves.

docs/onchain-analytics/raw/blockchain-in.note: TASK-009 — live keyless GET https://api.blockchain.info/stats (2026-07-29). Two facts rest on it. (1) It is the EMISSION source: bitcoinEmissionSat(n_blocks_total) reproduces totalbc bit-exactly, which is what pins n_blocks_total as a block COUNT rather than a tip height — a reading error of one block is 3.125 BTC = 0.000016% of supply and invisible to any plausibility check. (2) Together with the plaintext snapshot beside it, it is the evidence that /stats.totalbc sits at an INTEGER number of subsidies past the halving boundary while /q/totalbc does not. Re-recording it silently would turn a measurement back into an assumption.

docs/onchain-analytics/raw/blockscout-ad.note: Live keyless probe of GET /v1/get_address_info (USDC, chain 1, 2026-07-28). Carries the instructions[] array of LLM-directed imperatives with the caller address interpolated verbatim — the R-68e surface this task exists to close. basic_info.metadata is null here, which is why labels are read from data.metadata.tags.

docs/onchain-analytics/raw/blockscout-ch.note: Live keyless probe of GET https://mcp.blockscout.com/v1/get_chains_list (2026-07-28). Base of the generated coverage list: 100 chains / 47 testnets / 53 mainnets, every chain_id numeric. Re-recording it silently would move coverage without a diff.

docs/onchain-analytics/raw/blockscout-ho.note: Live keyless probe of GET /v1/direct_api_call (USDC holders, chain 1, 2026-07-28). Fixture source for the token.holders contract test, and the evidence that holder rows carry vendor free text in metadata.tags.

docs/onchain-analytics/raw/blockscout-in.note: L-12 — live keyless GET https://api.blockscout.com/api/json/config (2026-08-11). The VENDOR document behind the per-chain instance list in the issue: 100 chains under two disagreeing fields, `chains[id]` (what the PRO facade proxies to) and `chains_metadata[id].explorers[].hostedBy` (who actually runs the instance). The 26/24 first-party/third-party split and the 7 chains where the two fields name different explorers are read off it, and reading the wrong field silently routes Gnosis and Scroll at Etherscan-family hosts that do not speak /api/v2. Pinned because an egress decision over 24 third-party domains rests on which field was read.

docs/onchain-analytics/raw/blockscout-la.note: Live keyless probe of GET /v1/get_address_info (Binance Hot Wallet, chain 1, 2026-07-28). The address WITH labels: proves they live at data.metadata.tags[], not basic_info.metadata/name, both of which are null even here.

docs/onchain-analytics/raw/blockscout-pe.note: L-12 — OUR measurement of the instances the config file above names (2026-08-11): a keyless /api/v2/stats probe of all 50 hosts, and the decisive one, token.holders on five chains through the public instance against the same path through the PRO facade. Both routes fail and succeed together, and a warm instance made the facade fast on arbitrum seconds later — so the two share a backend index and the per-instance route is not an escape from the latency. That is what refutes the issue's fix-path item 2; re-recording it silently would turn a refutation back into an open option.

docs/onchain-analytics/raw/btc-crosschec.note: TASK-009 — coherent live snapshot of three plain-text surfaces (2026-07-29): blockchain.info /q/totalbc, /q/getblockcount and mempool.space /blocks/tip/height, taken back-to-back so they are comparable. It carries the decisive measurement of the task: /q/totalbc is 120092.8 subsidies past the halving boundary — FRACTIONAL, so it cannot be the halving formula nor a stale copy of one (a stale copy sits at an integer offset), and is therefore actually-claimed supply rather than emission. The whole two-field design of ChainSupply rests on that, and the task text it overrode prescribed the opposite.

docs/onchain-analytics/raw/defillama-cha.note: Two live keyless recordings of DeFiLlama's chain catalogue under its TWO naming vocabularies (GET /chains, legacy — the one GET /protocols speaks; GET /v2/chains, current — the one registry.data.json's vendors.defillama carries). src/adapters/defillama/chain-aliases.ts is GENERATED from it, and without that map protocol.tvl answers a confident `deployed: false, tvlUsd: 0` for 43 of 458 chains. The generator test compares the committed module against a regeneration from this evidence — editing BOTH would pass that check, which is what this pin closes.

docs/onchain-analytics/raw/defillama-dex.note: TASK-007 backlog item 6 — live keyless verification that DeFiLlama's `chain` echo equals the `vendors.defillama` name we send, for all 274 covered chains. It is the evidence that normalizeDexVolume's identity guard cannot misfire on a covered chain, and (incidentally) the first measured proof that a COVERED chain can return `total24h: null` — the justification for nullable aggregates, which until now cited a chain that is not covered. SUPERSEDED 2026-08-20 by the 014-32d re-probe: task 014-32a regenerated the registry, and the invariant this file served requires the probed set to equal the covered set. Kept and still pinned — a superseded measurement is evidence of what was true then.

Task 014-32d — live re-verification that DeFiLlama’s `chain` echo equals the `vendors.defillama` name we send, for every chain the coverage predicate admits. 272 chains, 0 mismatches. `defillama-dex-coverage.test.ts` asserts the probed set EQUALS the covered set, so this file and `registry.data.json` are one measurement in two places; re-recording either alone breaks the invariant loudly, which is the point.

TASK-007 task 007-2 — the vendor's own DEX-volume chain list, live-recorded keyless. src/adapters/defillama/dex-chains.ts is GENERATED from it, so this file decides which chains the engine advertises dex.volume.history on. The generator test compares the committed module against a regeneration from this evidence — editing BOTH would pass that check, which is precisely the gap this pin closes.

docs/onchain-analytics/raw/dexscreener-c.note: Task 014-32a — the per-chain DexScreener witness (R-33). 858 candidates (each row’s slug plus every alias, including the three curated for this task) probed for routability, then an echo pass over the routable ones; 69 candidates routable across 65 chains, 49 chains echoed. `gen-dexscreener-chains.ts` emits `src/adapters/dexscreener/chain-coverage.ts` from it, and `sync-chain-registry.ts` takes `vendors.dexscreener` from that module. Editing it silently would turn a per-chain measurement back into the three-entry spot-check that caused L-18.

packages/core/test/fixtures/defillama/de.note: L-5 — live-recorded response for a COVERED chain the vendor publishes nothing for, chart requested, 2026-07-28. It is the evidence that an empty chart with a series REQUESTED must count the whole window as missing (the five chains listed as `echoMatchedButNoVolume` in the echo probe), and that the vendor's three absence cases — key omitted, explicit null, real zero — are distinct and must stay so. Editing it would turn that measurement back into an assumption.

TASK-007 task 007-4 — live-recorded HTTP 200 zero-volume shape (narrower key set, change_1d null). It is the EVIDENCE that a missing aggregate must normalize to null rather than 0; hand-editing it would turn a measured vendor behaviour into an assumption.

TASK-007 / WI-17 (D-2) — live-recorded response for the includeSeries:false mode (excludeTotalDataChart=true), 2026-07-28. It answers a question that was previously a guess: the vendor KEEPS `totalDataChart` and sets it to an empty array rather than omitting it or sending null. That is what decides window/points/gapDays in that mode, so a silent edit here would rewrite a measured vendor behaviour into an assumption.

TASK-007 task 007-4 — live-recorded vendor response (trimmed to 120 daily points, protocols[] dropped). The gapless-92-point acceptance test rests on it; a silent edit would be indistinguishable from the vendor changing its answer.

packages/core/test/fixtures/defillama/ha.note: WI-52 — verbatim rows from the live keyless GET https://api.llama.fi/hacks and GET https://api.llama.fi/protocols, captured 2026-08-11. Pinned because the contract tests read the join keys and the four-way "no incidents" distinction straight out of it: an edit here would silently change what the measured 353/357 and 97/97 join rates in hacks-and-catalog.evidence.md refer to.
